title: The Changing Landscape of Hantavirus Infections: A Narrative Review of Epidemiology, Pathogenesis, and Countermeasures.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines mammalian orthohantaviruses (e.g., Hantaan, Seoul, Puumala, Dobrava-Belgrade, Sin Nombre, Andes viruses) causing human disease syndromes such as hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS), focusing on their epidemiology, pathogenesis, and countermeasures.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The supplied evidence does not report review type, databases, search dates, eligibility criteria, selection method, or included-study count; it is a narrative synthesis summarising developments over the past 5 years.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Endothelial dysfunction is the pathological hallmark of severe hantavirus disease, driven by VEGF sensitisation, Src kinase and RhoA pathway activation, pericyte infection, and dysregulated inflammatory responses including IL-6 trans-signalling. Diagnostic strategies rely on serology and molecular testing, while management remains predominantly supportive, with extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) improving survival in fulminant HCPS.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Critical gaps remain regarding determinants of person-to-person spread, long-term post-infection sequelae, and the absence of licenced broadly protective vaccines or specific antiviral therapies.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Future preparedness requires integrated surveillance frameworks combining ecological monitoring, genomic epidemiology, and clinical readiness within coordinated international public health strategies.

analysis.summary_en: This narrative review synthesises recent developments in hantavirus infections, focusing on mammalian orthohantaviruses (e.g., Hantaan, Seoul, Puumala, Dobrava-Belgrade, Sin Nombre, Andes viruses) and their associated human syndromes (HFRS, HCPS). Endothelial dysfunction underpins severe disease via VEGF sensitisation, Src/RhoA activation, pericyte infection, and IL-6 trans-signalling. Diagnostics rely on serology and molecular testing, while management remains supportive, with ECMO improving outcomes in fulminant HCPS. Key gaps include unresolved determinants of person-to-person transmission, long-term sequelae, and the lack of licenced vaccines or antivirals. Preparedness demands integrated surveillance linking ecological, genomic, and clinical data.

title: Interpretable Machine Learning for Mortality Risk Stratification in Hantavirus Infection: A Global Study Across Hemorrhagic Fever with Renal Syndrome and Hantavirus Cardiopulmonary Syndrome

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hantavirus infection is a rare but potentially fatal zoonosis, and early identification of patients at highest risk of death is essential for timely triage and resource allocation, yet robust risk stratification tools are lacking.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This retrospective supervised learning analysis used a global hantavirus epidemiology dataset of 10,000 patient records, including demographic, clinical, epidemiological, and treatment variables, to develop an interpretable machine learning framework for mortality risk stratification.
analysis.methods: Logistic regression, random forest, and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) models were trained and compared on a held-out test set using receiver operating characteristic-area under the curve (ROC-AUC), accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and Brier score, with preprocessing including identifier removal, missing-value handling, categorical and symptom encoding, feature selection, and class-imbalance correction.
analysis.main_results: Logistic regression achieved the highest discrimination with an ROC-AUC of 0.858 and the highest recall for mortality detection (0.741), but modest precision (0.321) and weaker calibration (Brier score 0.119); gradient boosting showed comparable discrimination (AUC 0.857) with better precision (0.511) and calibration (Brier score 0.076); random forest performed less well for mortality detection with markedly low recall (0.085).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study demonstrates that mortality risk in hantavirus infection can be modeled using routine clinical and epidemiological features, and supports the use of interpretable machine learning as a practical framework for early risk stratification.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that interpretable machine learning models could assist in early triage and resource allocation for hantavirus patients, particularly by prioritizing sensitivity, calibration, and transparency in clinical deployment.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and reliance on a single global dataset, which may affect generalisability; the evidence strength is moderate due to potential biases in data collection and model calibration challenges.

analysis.summary_en: This study developed an interpretable machine learning framework to stratify mortality risk among 10,000 global hantavirus cases, including both Hemorrhagic Fever with Renal Syndrome (64.6%) and Hantavirus Cardiopulmonary Syndrome (35.4%). Logistic regression achieved the highest discrimination (AUC 0.858) with strong sensitivity (recall 0.741) but modest precision (0.321), while gradient boosting offered better precision (0.511) and calibration (Brier score 0.076). Severity, syndrome type, viral load, age, and geography were the most informative predictors. The authors conclude that interpretable ML can support early triage and resource allocation, though deployment should prioritize sensitivity, calibration, and transparency over accuracy alone. The retrospective, single-dataset design and calibration limitations constrain generalisability, warranting external validation.

title: Spatial patterns of rodent-borne pathogens and ecological suitability of rodent-borne diseases in China.
